slot.subtopic: Range of a sin + b cos
slot.brief: Find the maximum and minimum of a cos θ + b sin θ and hence solve a given equation has no solution / find range.

stem: If the equation $3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta = 2\lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 2$ has a real solution for $\theta$, then the set of all possible values of $\lambda$ is

verdicts.working: 3sinθ+4cosθ has range [-5,5], so need -5 ≤ 2λ²-5λ-2 ≤ 5. Upper: 2λ²-5λ-7 ≤ 0 → (2λ-7)(λ+1) ≤ 0 → λ ∈ [-1, 7/2]. Lower: 2λ²-5λ+3 ≥ 0 → (2λ-3)(λ-1) ≥ 0 → λ ≤ 1 or λ ≥ 3/2. Intersection: [-1,1] ∪ [3/2, 7/2], matching option A; endpoints verified numerically.

working:
For any real $\theta$, the expression $a\sin\theta + b\cos\theta$ satisfies:
$$-\sqrt{a^2+b^2} \le a\sin\theta + b\cos\theta \le \sqrt{a^2+b^2}$$
Here, $a = 3$ and $b = 4$, so:
$$-\sqrt{3^2+4^2} \le 3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta \le \sqrt{3^2+4^2} \implies -5 \le 3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta \le 5$$
Therefore, the given equation has a real solution if and only if:
$$-5 \le 2\lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 2 \le 5$$

Solving the upper bound inequality:
$$2\lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 2 \le 5 \implies 2\lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 7 \le 0$$
$$(2\lambda - 7)(\lambda + 1) \le 0 \implies -1 \le \lambda \le \dfrac{7}{2} \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

Solving the lower bound inequality:
$$2\lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 2 \ge -5 \implies 2\lambda^2 - 5\lambda + 3 \ge 0$$
$$(2\lambda - 3)(\lambda - 1) \ge 0 \implies \lambda \le 1 \quad\text{or}\quad \lambda \ge \dfrac{3}{2} \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Taking the intersection of (1) and (2):
$$\lambda \in [-1, 1] \cup \left[\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{7}{2}\right]$$
